- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 1.0) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap upward revisions after 2–3 consecutive spikes.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile or mixed; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to initial forecast if sentiment swings >0.5.  
- If last 3–5 sentiment values are negative and price is trending up, model often lags; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.  
- In cases where true price rises sharply after a dip, model fails to capture the rebound; apply a “rebound multiplier” of +0.8 to forecast if sentiment turns positive after a negative spike.  
- Model tends to overestimate mean reversion in flat sentiment periods; reduce forecast slope if sentiment is neutral or low variance.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals, model overfits to recent noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values unless sentiment confirms trend.
